title: Surgical site infection bundle compliance after colorectal resection: a prospective observational study
subtitle: Element-level compliance and 30-day infection with post-discharge follow-up
statement: Surgical site infection followed 14 percent of about 380 colorectal resections in 2025, above the regional average, two years after a seven-element bundle was adopted. How reliably each element is delivered is unknown, and the working group disagrees about which elements matter. A prospective observational study would record each element at the time of surgery and follow every patient for 30 days, including after discharge.
whoAffected: Adults having elective and emergency colorectal resections, theatre and anaesthesia teams, surveillance nurses and the working group.
whatHurts: Wound infections cause pain, readmission, reoperation, delayed recovery and delayed adjuvant treatment; almost half appear after discharge.
currentPractice: The bundle is taught and expected but not recorded; surveillance counts infections without knowing which elements were given.
whyNow: An infection rate above the regional average, an unresolved argument about elements, and quality council approval for data collection.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient having colorectal surgery receives every bundle element that applies to them, and fewer patients develop a wound infection.
summary: Problem framed as a prospective observational study of bundle compliance and 30-day infection.
